questions.title: Binary runs under fixed counts
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result rederivation grounded in A. Wald and J. Wolfowitz, On a Test Whether Two Samples are from the Same Population, Annals of Mathematical Statistics 11 (1940), 147-162. Under the conditional null, fix integers n0,n1>=2 and draw uniformly from all binary sequences containing exactly n0 zeros and n1 ones. Let R be one plus the number of adjacent changes. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX Theory workspace, derive the exact finite-sample expectation and variance of R from indicator moments, explicitly treating overlapping and nonoverlapping adjacent-change pairs. State a justified large-sample scope for standardizing R and distinguish the resulting normal-approximation p-value from an exact finite-sample test. Do not assume adjacent-change indicators are independent, import the target formulas without derivation, or treat simulation as proof. Author exactly one model-owned Python estimator, est_binary_runs_summary, with run_estimator(request) implementing the frozen closed ABI below. The reported z statistic uses the uncorrected finite-sample centering and scaling derived in Theory, and its two-sided p-value uses the standard-normal approximation without a continuity correction. Exploratory Python or R may check enumeration and moments. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment executes exactly 4000 fresh uniformly shuffled sequences for each public count design (n0,n1)=(20,20) and (15,35), compares run-count moments and standardized-statistic behavior with the derived quantities, and reports Monte Carlo uncertainty. That assessment is implementation evidence, not a proof of the exact moments or asymptotic approximation. Source-code replication, novelty, sequential testing, general goodness-of-fit theory, and Lean formalization are not applicable.

primary_paper.title: On a Test Whether Two Samples are from the Same Population

request_fields.name: sequence
request_fields.meaning: One realized binary sequence whose run count is to be summarized conditionally on its observed zero and one counts.
request_fields.shape: one finite array of length 4 through 10000 with at least two zeros and at least two ones
request_fields.indexing: the supplied order is the sequence order; entries are exact JSON integers 0 or 1
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject nonarrays, booleans, floating values, strings, values outside {0,1}, lengths outside 4 through 10000, and sequences with fewer than two observations of either label. Reject rather than coerce, clip, drop, or reorder entries.

response_fields.name: n0
response_fields.meaning: The number of exact zero labels in sequence.
response_fields.edge_cases: At least two under every accepted request.
response_fields.normalization: sum(1 for x in sequence if x==0).

response_fields.name: n1
response_fields.meaning: The number of exact one labels in sequence.
response_fields.edge_cases: At least two under every accepted request.
response_fields.normalization: sum(1 for x in sequence if x==1).

response_fields.name: runs
response_fields.meaning: The number of maximal constant-label blocks in the supplied order.
response_fields.indexing: adjacent pairs are sequence[i-1],sequence[i] for i=1,...,n-1
response_fields.edge_cases: Includes the initial run, so it is one plus the adjacent-change count.

response_fields.name: mean_runs
response_fields.meaning: The exact conditional-null expectation of runs for the observed n0 and n1.
response_fields.normalization: The exact formula derived in the authoritative Theory workspace under uniform ordering conditional on n0,n1.

response_fields.name: variance_runs
response_fields.meaning: The exact conditional-null variance of runs for the observed n0 and n1.
response_fields.edge_cases: Strictly positive and finite for every accepted request.
response_fields.normalization: The exact formula derived in the authoritative Theory workspace under uniform ordering conditional on n0,n1.

response_fields.name: z_statistic
response_fields.meaning: The uncorrected standardized run count using the exact finite-sample conditional mean and variance.
response_fields.edge_cases: Finite for every accepted request; no continuity correction is applied.

response_fields.name: two_sided_p_value
response_fields.meaning: The two-sided standard-normal approximation p-value for the uncorrected z statistic.
response_fields.edge_cases: Finite and in [0,1]; it is approximate rather than an exact permutation-tail probability.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly sequence and the response contains exactly n0,n1,runs,mean_runs,variance_runs,z_statistic,two_sided_p_value. Missing or extra fields and invalid values are rejected rather than ignored or coerced.
Replacing every label x by 1-x swaps n0 and n1 but leaves runs, mean_runs, variance_runs, z_statistic, and two_sided_p_value unchanged.
Reversing sequence leaves the complete response unchanged.
Repeated calls on the same request return identical JSON values, do not mutate the request, and evaluate only the fixed-count binary runs summary specified here.

empirical_claims.meaning: Before outcomes, freeze the two public fixed-count designs, one seed per design, exactly 4000 fresh uniform permutations per design, one accepted-estimator invocation per replicate, and all Monte Carlo decision rules.

For each public count design, compare empirical run-count mean and variance with the exact conditional quantities and assess the standardized statistic's mean, variance, and nominal 0.05 two-sided normal-approximation rejection frequency with Monte Carlo uncertainty.

The confirmatory result concerns only uniformly shuffled fixed-count binary sequences at the two declared count designs. It does not prove the exact formulas, establish an exact finite-sample p-value, or cover dependent orderings, estimated cut points, other sample sizes, source replication, novelty, or formal correctness.
